review.summary: Phoenix is currently in a research-only phase with significant gaps in its architecture and controls. The lack of settled outcomes and verified observations, along with the inability to promote candidates without meeting strict empirical baselines, leads to the decision to reject its current implementation.
top_technical_reasons: No verified BCS observations to support claims.
Storage backends are not fully connected, limiting data access.
Fact-check stage is injectable but not yet canonical, raising concerns about reliability.
The orchestrator is not yet integrated into the Streamlit runtime, affecting operational readiness.
review.candidate_safety: The current implementation lacks sufficient safety checks and has not undergone acceptance testing, raising concerns about its reliability and safety in production.

next_experiments.hypothesis: Establishing verified BCS observations will enhance the credibility of the system.

next_experiments.why_it_is_informative: This will provide insights into the reliability of the system and its ability to meet empirical baselines.
